issue.title: Guzzle formats cookie-strings incorrectly
issue.body:
Guzzle formats cookies-strings as semi-colon `;` separated cookie-pairs, however, [RFC 6265](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6265) seems to require that they be separated by `;` with a space after the semi-colon. 

First, from [Syntax](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6265#section-4.2.1):

> 4.2.1.  Syntax
> 
>   The user agent sends stored cookies to the origin server in the
>    Cookie header.  If the server conforms to the requirements in
>    Section 4.1 (and the user agent conforms to the requirements in
>    Section 5), the user agent will send a Cookie header that conforms to
>    the following grammar:
> 
>   cookie-header = "Cookie:" OWS cookie-string OWS
>   cookie-string = cookie-pair *( ";" SP cookie-pair )

And, from [The Cookie Header](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6265#section-5.4):

> 1.  Serialize the cookie-list into a cookie-string by processing each
>      cookie in the cookie-list in order:
>    1.  Output the cookie's name, the %x3D ("=") character, and the
>         cookie's value.
>    2.  If there is an unprocessed cookie in the cookie-list, output
>         the characters %x3B and %x20 ("; ").

The [Examples](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6265#section-3.1) section shows it separated by `;` as well.

issue.title: PHP 7.3: use hrtime() instead of microtime()
issue.body:
**Guzzle version(s) affected**: 6.3.3

**Description**  
Consider switching from microtime() to hrtime(), available in PHP 7.3. It provides a monotonic timestamp rather than a realtime timestamp.

**How to reproduce**  
Using microtime() is unsafe e.g. on a DST crossover or whenever the system time is adjusted, since the timestamps aren't relative to each other.

It is used in the CurlMultiHandler and the `on_stats` option.

Apart from needing to keep support for < 7.3, the change here should be without a BC break.

Treat plus symbols from parsed query string as spaces
issue.body:
Part of a behat acceptance test I'm working on involves going through google's oauth process.

At one point in the flow google responds with a redirect to a url that uses a plus symbol as a url encoded space. Instead of treating this symbol as a space guzzle considers it to be a literal plus symbol, and encodes it as such.

Here are the two urls:

```
Location:  https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/auth?scope=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.googleapis.com%2Fauth%2Fuserinfo.profile+https%3A%2F%2Fwww.googleapis.com%2Fauth%2Fuserinfo.email&response_type=code&redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%2Foauth2callback&client_id=707579192915-l6nqvq0vp96se8s0puojr42uvfo9d9fr.apps.googleusercontent.com&hl=en-GB&from_login=1&as=-54afd41634aa446e&auth=DQAAAIYAAACcC1jTQfPVqofuRSbzlbbzXudBzK_JTt792Le9D-k8HUFiaN3FFhdVjTF-Wx3bTeGtpK4PIWVgeg4eLhIhs-AEtP0dIfB0FIxid14-i6_WP_hxpDA-szymr1zFszLA86p4-FQUgBZ_-YrkmJuAwffH0JIxgUG9bkkNmF8kVKzWH6D0IPxdyhG-HouSnbKO6dU
Generated: https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/auth?scope=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.googleapis.com%2Fauth%2Fuserinfo.profile%2Bhttps%3A%2F%2Fwww.googleapis.com%2Fauth%2Fuserinfo.email&response_type=code&redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%2Foauth2callback&client_id=707579192915-l6nqvq0vp96se8s0puojr42uvfo9d9fr.apps.googleusercontent.com&hl=en-GB&from_login=1&as=-54afd41634aa446e&auth=DQAAAIYAAACcC1jTQfPVqofuRSbzlbbzXudBzK_JTt792Le9D-k8HUFiaN3FFhdVjTF-Wx3bTeGtpK4PIWVgeg4eLhIhs-AEtP0dIfB0FIxid14-i6_WP_hxpDA-szymr1zFszLA86p4-FQUgBZ_-YrkmJuAwffH0JIxgUG9bkkNmF8kVKzWH6D0IPxdyhG-HouSnbKO6dU
```

The first one is from the `Location` header and the second one is the one requested by Guzzle, taken at the point the curl handle is created. Here's the diff of the two urls:

![Diff](https://dl.dropbox.com/u/176888/Screenshots/2012-07-19-diff.jpg.jpg)

If the second url is used then google treats the plus symbol as a literal plus, which causes an error as it's expecting a space delimited field.

issue.title: Problem with 302 redirect and Auth on initial (but not redirected) link
issue.body:
I am downloading a file with Guzzle 6.2.0. The original url, via https, requires Digest authorization, then returns a 302 redirect to another url on a different domain (http) that does NOT require authorization.

When I try to use Guzzle to download the file following redirects automatically, Guzzle makes the initial connection, gets back a 401, sends again with the correct authorization headers, gets back the 302 redirect--all good. 

Then it tries to send the same exact Authorization headers with the request to the new url, which gets back a 400 bad request, I assume because the redirected URL does not expect authorization.

I have gotten around this by capturing the redirect url via an `on_stats` function, setting `allow_redirects` to false, and creating a completely separate request for the redirected url. But it seems that there should be a better way to handle this.

This is not my area of expertise--does it EVER make sense to send the same auth headers for a 302 redirect to a separate domain?

issue.title: (Lack of) cache invalidation
issue.body:
Thought of a an issue introduced by #250 (and made visible in #251), and similar one that existed before: cache invalidation.

The existing issue is that `POST`, `PUT` and `DELETE` requests don't invalidate any cached responses from the same URI. So a `DELETE` request where there's a fresh cached copy will see a `GET` request use the cache rather than being forced to issue a new request and presumably see a `404` response. The `stale-if-error` directive would also see a `GET` received a stale cached version if there's a problem.

To get round this I think the cache storage needs to keep a list of URIs and all their keys, it can then invalidate the cache for a particular URI when required.

The new issue is that a `404` etc response doesn't see the cached copy removed. So if  I'm using the `stale-if-error` directive and I get a `200` response, then a `404`, then a `500`, the last request is going to see the original cached `200` response.

When were you planning to release the next version? I'll see if I can get a PR done soon.

issue.title: Proxy syntax not consistent across handlers
issue.body:
**Guzzle version(s) affected**: Current git master (3a0543e4f589e21e8d65b984e544967c9de2b8b2 / 7.2.0)
**PHP version**: 7.4.12
**cURL version**: 7.64.0

**Description**  

The correct proxy syntax is not consistent across handlers. This is problematic, because certain request options automatically switch to another handler (namely `stream`).

**How to reproduce**  

```php
<?php

use GuzzleHttp\Client;
use GuzzleHttp\Psr7\Request;

require('vendor/autoload.php');

$client = new Client();

echo "####################".PHP_EOL;
echo "Stream: false".PHP_EOL;
echo "####################".PHP_EOL;

try {
	$request = new Request('GET', 'http://www.example.com');
	$response = $client->send($request, [
		'stream' => false,
	]);
	var_dump(substr($response->getBody(), 0, 100));
} catch (\Exception $e) {
	echo $e.PHP_EOL;
}

echo PHP_EOL;
echo "####################".PHP_EOL;
echo "Stream: true".PHP_EOL;
echo "####################".PHP_EOL;

try {
	$request = new Request('GET', 'http://www.example.com');
	$response = $client->send($request, [
		'stream' => true,
	]);
	var_dump(substr($response->getBody(), 0, 100));
} catch (\Exception $e) {
	echo $e.PHP_EOL;
}
```

With `HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:8888`:

issue.title: additionalParameters:false not enforced
issue.body:
From docs:

> additionalProperties: (array) This attribute defines a schema for all properties that are not explicitly defined in an object type definition. If specified, the value MUST be a schema or a boolean. If false is provided, no additional properties are allowed beyond the properties defined in the schema. The default value is an empty schema which allows any value for additional properties.

This means that setting `additionalParameters` to `false` would effectively discard any undefined properties that have been found in the incoming data ( _model data sanitisation_ ).

This however is not a case with current version of Guzzle and both XML and JSON visitors will happily throw all incoming properties into Model.

issue.title: Feature request: MockPlugin uses mock responses only
issue.body:
I make regular use of mock responses (both http messages and curl exceptions) and occasionally run in to problems in CI environments where I've forgotten to add a mock response.

Tests depending on mock responses may pass locally as requests lacking mock responses succeed by luck not design (such as a test-related host resolving locally but not on travis).

If I do forget to add all the required mock responses such that tests pass locally by chance but fail on one or more CI environments, I can sort things out by carefully tracing the requests that are made and the responses that are required,

This can, however, take some time.

I would be great if the MockPlugin could be told to only use queued responses, throwing an exception if there are no responses in the queue.

Since it is probably best practice within tests to mock all responses to all requests, it makes sense that the mock plugin throws an exception if it is passed a request for which it has no response.
